metadata.name: Localization
metadata.description: Guides > Adding a new language. Six sections + TOC + next-reads. Corrects two factual errors from the earlier draft: there is no `jui localize` CLI (it's all `jui build`), and Android does NOT get a StringManager.kt (it emits res/values[-lang]/strings.xml natively). Walks the bilingual shape, namespace derivation, per-platform output asymmetry, Web-only reactive language switching, the 5 mechanical steps to add a locale, and current limits (no plurals, no pseudo-loc, %@/%s interpolation auto-convert).

methods.name: onAppear
methods.description: Seed nextReadLinks from the module-scope NEXT_READ_ENTRIES catalog (two rows: next_spec_first -> /guides/writing-your-first-spec, next_concepts_data_binding -> /concepts/data-binding) and stamp currentLanguage from StringManager.language. Each row's titleKey / descriptionKey is resolved through StringManager with the guides_localization_ namespace prefix.

methods.name: onNavigate
methods.description: Client-side navigation via router.push(url). Destinations are the spec-mapped URLs enumerated in transitions: /, /guides/writing-your-first-spec, /concepts/data-binding.

vars.name: nextReadLinks
vars.description: Two closing 'read next' cards pointing at /guides/writing-your-first-spec and /concepts/data-binding. Seeded by onAppear from the NEXT_READ_ENTRIES static catalog and re-seeded by onToggleLanguage.

notes: Live Guides entry. Flip GUIDES_ENTRIES row for 'localization' to 'live' in HomeViewModel when shipping.

Six sections: (1) bilingual shape with JSON excerpt, (2) namespace naming rules with derivation table, (3) per-platform output (iOS StringManager.swift + Localizable.strings, Android strings.xml only — NO StringManager.kt, Web StringManager.ts), (4) Web-only reactive setLanguage with real TS toggle example, (5) five-step locale addition with JSON + bash excerpts per step, (6) limits (no plurals / no pseudo-loc / %@ ↔ %s auto-convert).

Corrects prior false claims: 'jui localize' CLI does not exist (localisation is part of jui build), 'No per-platform .strings / strings.xml maintenance' misstates Android reality, 'whole screen re-renders on setLanguage' is true for Web only.
Deprecated strings: section_add_* / section_scale_* / toc_row_add / toc_row_scale remain in strings.json as unreferenced dead entries to minimise cross-session merge risk.

2026-08-31 — section_naming_body gains the 1.7.23 wrapper-literal strictness. Measured three ways on one fixture, one variable each: with a same-file 'function str' composing 'home_' + its argument, v1.7.23 reports str('farewel') as composing an undeclared 'home_farewel' while str('greeting') resolves; the same fixture on v1.7.22 is clean; and moving the wrapper into a sibling file and importing it returns v1.7.23 to clean. The published sentence about this site being unaffected is measured rather than assumed — jui lint-strings --usage prints the same 1001 unused / 74 undeclared on v1.7.20 and v1.7.23, and the accessors here are methods (this.s(...)) rather than free functions, which is the reason. An earlier run of that fixture reported both calls as missing; the cause was the fixture naming its keys 'home_greeting' inside namespace 'home', so the flat key was 'home_home_greeting' and the wrapper's composition genuinely did not exist.

2026-09-25 — v1.8.119: `jui lint-strings --usage` no longer counts references from test code as usage, and says where it looked. Measured on this site under 1.8.118 and 1.8.119: the two new lines are 'usage scanned 719 source file(s), excluded 0 as test code' and 'test code (web): test runner defaults: *.test.*, *.spec.*, __tests__/'. Where test code is on each platform, and lint.stringsUsageTestPaths, are read from lint_strings_usage.py; the behaviour itself was not exercised on a fixture with test-only references.

2026-09-28 — v1.9.0: the images bullet. Measured on web by building a copy of this site with four Images under 1.8.120 and 1.9.0: no alt and `"alt": ""` both render `alt=""` on both versions, a strings.json key renders `alt={$s.homeHeroTitle}`, and a tappable image with no alt keeps `alt=""` with no build line (1.9.0 adds role="button", tabIndex and Enter / Space to it). That iOS and Android read alt from 1.9.0, its spellings accessibilityLabel / contentDescription, and the native build naming an operable image without one are the SSoT declaration's, not measured here.

2026-10-03 — pin v1.9.8: section_naming_body gains the 1.9.8 key resolution. Measured on web on a scratch copy of this site: concepts/hot-reload's title written as its literal English text printed the literal under 1.9.7 and rendered `{$s.conceptsHotReloadTitle}` under 1.9.8, with 1 generated file differing between the arms. The same layout given '8. In CI', the text of a guides_testing key, stayed literal under 1.9.8, so the search is own-section only. iOS / Android and the empty-text rule are the orchestrator's word.

2026-10-04 — pin v1.9.10. Measured on web on a scratch copy of this site: a plural entry with en forms and no ja builds with exit 0 at 1.9.9 and exits 1 at 1.9.10 with '[ERROR] <key>: a plural entry needs its own forms for every language of this strings.json — missing ja (languages here: en, ja)…'. The iOS category language and the kjui strings.xml region are the orchestrator's 1.9.10 notice, not measured here (no iOS / Android lane). This site has 0 plural entries, so its own clean build says nothing about plurals.
